messages.author: 17d9c7a6e1a581b8
messages.subject: sharing code in Py/R/CmdStan: effective_sample_size
parts:
Hi,

There are many opportunities for eliminating extra implementations of identical
functionality in PyStan/RStan/CmdStan. For example, there are three
implementations of effective_sample_size (and split_potential_scale_reduction).

I'd like to get that number down to two by eliminating the version in PyStan
and just using the functions in stan/mcmc/chains.hpp from Python.

Python's Rcpp, called Cython, handles C++ vectors without any trouble. So the
main challenge is just what to do about moving between a C++ vector and an Eigen
VectorXd. As this seems like it might be a general concern, I thought I'd raise
the question of an appropriate strategy on the list.

One thought I had is that in the areas where a simple conversion is required,
Stan might expose a function that accepts a vector in addition to a version
that accepts a VectorXd.

Thanks,

-a

messages.author: 2c952029259d7788
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] sharing code in Py/R/CmdStan: effective_sample_size
parts:
On Tue, Jan 28, 2014 at 3:20 PM, Allen Riddell <a...@ariddell.org> wrote:
Python's Rcpp, called Cython, handles C++ vectors without any trouble. So the
main challenge is just what to do about moving between a C++ vector and an Eigen
VectorXd. As this seems like it might be a general concern, I thought I'd raise
the question of an appropriate strategy on the list.

One thought I had is that in the areas where a simple conversion is required,
Stan might expose a function that accepts a vector in addition to a version
that accepts a VectorXd.

An alternative to converting to std::vector<> would be to use minieigen[1], pyeigen[2], or similar Eigen bindings for Python, which provide similar functionality to RcppEigen[3], which provides R bindings for Eigen.  (These are broader than just VectorXd, and may not require a copy to an STL vector, which could save time for large vectors.)

Last I checked, the two Python bindings I mentioned were still under development, but they may have matured by now.  Even if they haven't fully matured, the VectorXd bindings/parts are probably stable.  I've used RcppEigen and it's pretty stable.

Sorry in advance if you've already considered this and I'm just stating the obvious. :-)

Ido

[1] https://pypi.python.org/pypi/minieigen
[2] https://launchpad.net/pyeigen
[3] http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/RcppEigen/index.html

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] sharing code in Py/R/CmdStan: effective_sample_size
parts:
This was, by the way, one of the reasons I thought
std::vector interfaces would be easier and more portable.

What Michael's suggesting is probably the path of least
resistance and shouldn't be inefficient (other than to
compile).

A more idiomatic approach within C++ would be to define the
interfaces in terms of iterators. A more generic way to do
it with references to container arguments would be to template
out the container type and just use accessors (for example, []
works for arrays, standard vectors, C++11 arrays, Eigen vectors, and
many of the Boost sequence containers). The cost is that the code's a
bit more complex, which is why we've (or at least I've) tended not
to do it that way. But I think we're all getting better at C++,
so maybe this shouldn't be such a hurdle any more.

- Bob
